question: Should OpenClaw support this workflow-completion use case through a new internal `session:end` hook, or should the existing typed plugin `session_end` lifecycle hook be the documented supported surface?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but root policy favors plugins for optional runtime extension while the issue requests an internal HOOK.md automation contract; choosing the permanent public surface is a maintainer product/API decision.

options.title: Document plugin `session_end` as the supported surface
options.body: Use the existing typed plugin lifecycle hook for orchestration integrations and close or narrow internal-hook requests once docs make that boundary explicit.

options.title: Add a narrow internal `session:end` event
options.body: Define, document, and wire one internal event across the relevant completion paths with tests for reset, cron, subagent, and shutdown semantics.

options.title: Keep issue blocked on linked PR review
options.body: Defer this issue until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 is refreshed, proven, and either landed or closed.

recommendation.title: Document plugin `session_end` as the supported surface
recommendation.body: Use the existing typed plugin lifecycle hook for orchestration integrations and close or narrow internal-hook requests once docs make that boundary explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is tied to the active hook/session-memory repair branch and the plugin hook boundary most directly implicated by this choice.
